gdeltGeoMeta.provider: The GDELT Project — Global Knowledge Graph (GKG) 2.1 fifteen-minute feeds
gdeltGeoMeta.attribution: GDELT terms of use require citation: The GDELT Project (https://www.gdeltproject.org/)
gdeltGeoMeta.geoApiNote: The GDELT GEO 2.0 API (api.gdeltproject.org/api/v2/geo/geo) answered HTTP 404 for its own documented example URLs at implementation time and is treated as retired; this pipeline reproduces its documented point-mode semantics from the supported keyless GKG 2.1 fifteen-minute files that powered it.

titleEnrichment.query: (theme:ARMEDCONFLICT OR theme:TERROR OR theme:REBELLION OR theme:INSURGENCY OR theme:VIOLENT_UNREST OR theme:CEASEFIRE OR theme:PEACEKEEPING)

gdeltGeoMeta.selection: Ingests the newest 2 successfully downloaded fifteen-minute GKG 2.1 slots for both the English web and machine-translated collections (walking back up to 6 slots per collection when the newest files are not yet published), keeps rows carrying at least one of the documented conflict themes [ARMEDCONFLICT, TERROR, REBELLION, INSURGENCY, VIOLENT_UNREST, CEASEFIRE, PEACEKEEPING] in V2ENHANCEDTHEMES, retains only sub-national location mentions (GDELT location types 2-5) within 300 characters of a conflict-theme mention, deduplicates by normalized article URL plus location identity, then caps at 600 mentions ranked by matched-theme count, spatial precision class, proximity, and recency. Country-level mentions (type 1) are out of scope by design and reported as an informational count rather than an omission.
gdeltGeoMeta.caveat: GDELT geolocated news points are locations mentioned inside news text within roughly a sentence or two (a documented 300-character window, measured with GDELT-supplied character offsets) of automated conflict-theme tags. They describe the geography of media attention, not verified incident locations, and a point is never evidence that an event occurred at that place. GDELT geocoding, machine translation, and theme assignment are fully automated and error-prone; city/landmark coordinates come from GDELT gazetteer matching, while US-state and world admin-1 matches plot at the centroid of that entire division as coarse symbolic placement, never at an incident site. The GKG feed does not supply per-article publication times: slotTime is the fifteen-minute monitoring slot in which the mention was captured and seenAt exists only where a DOC API cross-reference matched the exact article URL. Article headlines are not part of the GKG feed either and appear only through that same opportunistic cross-reference. Absence of coverage is not absence of conflict.
